title: Service Contracts: termination for default after a long suspension, and expiry at term end
content:
## Scope
This policy of the Aurelia Hanse Line (AHL) Service Contracts product governs two ways a contract ends other than by the customer's own notice: termination by the line for default after a prolonged suspension, and expiry at the end of the term.

## Formal clauses
1. A contract that stays suspended for the tier's suspension period, in calendar days, may be terminated by the line for default, and every outstanding shortfall stays payable.
2. A contract that reaches its expiry date expires, and the term-end shortfall and the term-end rebate are then settled under the Service Contracts shortfall and volume rebate rules.

## Effect on the contract
| Event | Status before | Status after | Carried out by |
|---|---|---|---|
| Termination for default | suspended | terminated | the line |
| Expiry | active | expired | the system, at the end of the term |

## Points of judgement
**Must the line terminate once the suspension period has run?** No. The clause says the line may terminate the contract for default; it does not oblige it to.

**Is an unpaid shortfall cancelled by a termination for default?** No. Every outstanding shortfall stays payable after the termination.

**Hypothetical 40-day suspension period.** A contract suspended since 2026-03-01 and never reinstated has, by 2026-05-01, stayed suspended for well over 40 calendar days, so the line may terminate it for default. On 2026-03-20 it has been suspended for 19 days, and the period has not yet run.

**A contract reinstated before the period has run.** It has not stayed suspended for the tier's period, so this clause does not open termination for default.

**What follows expiry?** The contract's term-end shortfall and term-end rebate are settled under the shortfall and volume rebate rules of Service Contracts.
